skill: Applying statistical and analytical tools and techniques
expected_level_description: You can: - lead the development of valuable statistical insights and reports - identify and apply a range of statistical and analytical techniques and tools, and support others in applying them - quality assure statistical techniques and analytical outputs across a team - engage with stakeholders and share statistical and analytical techniques to increase understanding and trust

skill: Communicating between the technical and non-technical
expected_level_description: You can: - listen to and interpret the needs of technical and non-technical stakeholders, and manage their expectations - manage active and reactive communication - support or host difficult discussions within the team or with diverse senior stakeholders

You can: - work with stakeholders to identify and address ethical and privacy concerns - demonstrate and communicate how data ethical issues fit into the wider organisational context - research developments in data ethics and privacy to improve compliance and processes - assess and constructively challenge proposed data ethics policies

You can: - advocate for effective data governance and data management policies and guidelines within your team and across your organisation - monitor and improve data management practices in your team - help define, develop and support the use of data management tools, procedures and methods in compliance with data governance policies

You can: - plan the framework of an analytical data model based on appropriate data sources - support the implementation of data models using appropriate tools and systems - ensure your team understands the importance of data quality and modelling

You can: - use a range of data visualisations to simplify a complex story - adapt a story to the needs of multidisciplinary stakeholders - advise and support others in developing inclusive, accessible data visualisations that recognise different user needs - suggest improvements to data visualisation processes and standards to increase efficiency and quality

You can: - lead and support others in using data to deliver business impact - define and communicate the scope of the business impact you deliver so the value is clear - identify opportunities to develop data products that deliver business impact - develop and deliver scalable data products that align to organisational priorities and enable decision making

You can: - design and implement the analytical approach, including code, using appropriate standards and tests - lead collaboration to review and improve analytical approaches, including shared code - guide others in producing analytical approach documentation, identifying improvements

You can: - identify and define a problem statement - apply and share project management methodologies, including tools and techniques - plan and implement different stages of the data project life cycle - communicate progress of data projects with stakeholders - adapt teams' ways of working to deliver different project outcomes and requirements

You can: - analyse how a service fits into care pathways across organisations - work with clinicians, care staff, and patients to shape digital services - explain the effect of digital decisions on care, safety, and staff workload

You can: - lead data protection impact assessments and information sharing agreements - advise teams on lawful basis, consent, confidentiality, and retention - investigate incidents and recommend improvements
You can: - define data quality rules and measures - work with data providers to fix the root causes of poor quality

You can: - design pseudonymisation and linkage methods that keep identifiers separate from analysis data - assess the re-identification risk of a data set or publication and choose suitable controls - advise teams on safe settings, such as trusted research environments
You can: - find and use the right codes for a data item or form - use terminology browsers and reference sets
You can: - recognise and challenge behaviour that excludes others - consider different needs when you plan your work
